`README.md`:

```md
# AREA — Anti-Reverse-Engineer-Anything

> You ship software. Other people (and a growing number of AI agents) take it
> apart to figure out how it works, then rebuild it for free. AREA makes that
> job annoying enough that most of them give up.

**AREA** is a defensive toolkit for anyone who ships closed-source or licensed
software and would rather it stayed closed. It's built specifically to blunt
[REA (`reverse-engineer-anything`)](https://github.com/morluto/rea) and the tools
it leans on — Ghidra, Hopper, IDA, Kuna, Frida, LLDB, GDB, CDP/DevTools, Wakaru —
so that when one of those agents points at your app, it comes back with
"couldn't determine" instead of a working clone.

Think of it as the counter-skill to `reverse-engineer-anything`: REA works by
reading the information you accidentally left in your build and poking at the
channels you left open. AREA just... removes that information and closes those
channels.

## Why this exists

Reverse engineering used to be a niche skill. Now anyone can ask an AI agent to
do it. The agent runs `analyze_javascript_application` on your Electron app,
`open_binary` + `analyze_function` on your native binary, or captures your live
web app into a bundle — then hands back a reconstruction. The frustrating part:
it mostly works because the build gives it everything it needs for free.

AREA is the fix. Same tools, pointed the other way.

## How it works, in one breath

REA (and everything like it) leans on three things:

1. **Your artifacts are readable** — plaintext JavaScript, source maps, symbols,
   plaintext strings, embedded build metadata.
2. **Your runtime is open** — DevTools/CDP ports, `--inspect`, debuggers and
   Frida can just walk in.
3. **Your builds are predictable** — same identifiers every release, so diffing
   two versions is trivial.

AREA attacks each one. Full breakdown here: [references/threat-model.md](references/threat-model.md).

## REA tool → what AREA does about it

| REA surface | AREA counter |
| --- | --- |
| `analyze_javascript_application`, `recover_javascript_sources`, `trace_application_feature` | Obfuscate + mangle, drop source maps, compile to V8 bytecode or native addons |
| `compare_application_versions`, `compare_javascript_export_shapes` | Re-obfuscate every release with a fresh seed so nothing lines up |
| `inspect_electron_fuses`, `list_electron_targets`, CDP debug | Flip the fuses (`--inspect`, `RunAsNode`, `NODE_OPTIONS` off; asar integrity on) |
| `open_binary` + `analyze_function` + strings/xrefs | OLLVM/garble/goldberg, string encryption, control-flow flattening, packing |
| `inspect_binary_layout`, `inspect_pe_imports`, `inspect_native_exports`, `inspect_elf_notes`, `inspect_macho` | Strip symbols/build-id, resolve imports dynamically, hide visibility, export almost nothing |
| `observe_native_calls`, `start_gdb_session`, Rizin | Anti-debug, drop `get-task-allow`, hardened runtime |
| `start_frida_session`, `load_frida_script` | Anti-Frida: watch port 27042, scan for agent/gadget, ptrace guard |
| `list_browser_targets`, `capture_browser_scenario`, `observe_web_execution`, WebMCP | Anti-CDP, `navigator.webdriver` guard, no WebMCP manifest, strict CSP |
| `export_environment_bundle` (AgentEnv) | Thin client + server-side logic + auth + streaming |
| `inspect_go_binary`, `inspect_rust_binary`, `inspect_python_pyc`, `inspect_il2cpp_metadata`, `inspect_sqlite_database` | Strip `.go.buildinfo` / `.dep-v0` / `.pyc`, encrypt IL2CPP metadata and DBs |
| Network captures (HAR/SAZ/mitmproxy/PCAP) | Certificate pinning + application-layer encryption |

## Quick start

Grab the track for your stack, apply it, then check your work by pointing REA at
the result.

```sh
# JavaScript / Electron
node scripts/obfuscate-javascript.mjs ./dist ./dist-obf --seed 0x1234abcd
node scripts/harden-electron.js --fuses --no-sourcemaps

# Native
./scripts/strip-native.sh ./app.bin --upx

# Go
./scripts/harden-go.sh ./cmd/myapp

# Rust
./scripts/harden-rust.sh --release

# Web headers + anti-automation
node scripts/generate-csp.cjs
```

Then verify, if you have REA handy:

```sh
npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application /abs/path/to/app --json
```

A hardened build should come back as `coverage: incomplete` or `unknown` — not
recovered logic, names, routes, or strings.

## Scripts

| Script | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `scripts/obfuscate-javascript.mjs` | `javascript-obfuscator` with AREA defaults — flattening, string arrays, self-defending, no source map |
| `scripts/harden-electron.js` | Flips Electron fuses, turns on asar integrity, strips source maps |
| `scripts/strip-native.sh` | Strips symbols/build-id/`.dep-v0`, optional UPX pack |
| `scripts/harden-go.sh` | garble build with literal obfuscation + `-trimpath` + build-id clear |
| `scripts/harden-rust.sh` | Release build + symbol/`.dep-v0` stripping |
| `scripts/anti-debug.h` | C/C++ anti-debug, anti-Frida, anti-LLDB/GDB primitives |
| `scripts/integrity-check.js` | Runtime SHA-256 tamper check |
| `scripts/generate-csp.cjs` | Strict CSP + anti-automation headers and snippet |

## Installing as a skill

Pull this into an agent and drop it next to `reverse-engineer-anything`, so
hardening happens by default whenever software gets built:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/<your-org>/anti-reverse-engineer-anything.git
# copy SKILL.md + references/ + scripts/ into the agent's skills directory
```

## A few honest caveats

- **This is deterrence, not a vault.** Obfuscation and anti-debug make reverse
  engineering slow and unrewarding; they don't make it impossible. The real win
  is that casual cloners and evidence-bound AI agents stall out. A determined
  human with time and budget will always get through eventually.
- **Keep real secrets on the server.** No amount of obfuscation protects a key or
  algorithm you shipped to the client.
- **Mind your distribution channel.** Packers and heavy anti-debug can trip
  antivirus heuristics and app-store review, so test before you ship.
- **Stay on your own lawn.** Use this only on software you own or are authorized
  to protect.

---
name: anti-reverse-engineer-anything
description: >-
  Harden software so AI reverse-engineering agents (REA, "reverse-engineer-anything",
  Ghidra/Hopper/IDA/Kuna, Frida, LLDB, GDB, CDP/DevTools, Wakaru) fail or stall when they
  try to decompile, clone, or fingerprint your shipped app. Use when building or shipping
  proprietary/closed-source software, Electron/Node/JavaScript apps, native binaries
  (C/C++/Rust/Go), mobile apps, or web apps that must resist decompilation, cloning,
  source recovery, source-map recovery, string extraction, import/export enumeration,
  build-metadata fingerprinting, runtime instrumentation, debugger attach, Frida hooking,
  DevTools/remote-debugging access, and AgentEnv bundle capture. Applies obfuscation,
  control-flow flattening, string encryption, symbol stripping, packers, anti-debug,
  anti-Frida, anti-tamper integrity checks, Electron fuses, asar integrity, cert pinning,
  and metadata stripping. NOT for malware evasion or defeating license-check legal
  enforcement on others' software; use only on software you own or are authorized to protect.

# AREA — Anti-Reverse-Engineer-Anything

Counter-skill to `reverse-engineer-anything` (REA) and the wider class of AI-assisted
reverse-engineering tooling. Where REA recovers readable source, names, strings, imports,
call graphs, and runtime behavior from a shipped artifact, AREA removes the assumptions
REA depends on, so a REA-driven agent hits dead ends instead of conclusions.

## When to apply

Apply this skill **before shipping** any software you own and do not want cloned,
decompiled, or fingerprinted. It is most valuable for:

- Electron / Node.js / JavaScript apps (desktop + web bundles)
- Native binaries: C, C++, Objective-C, Rust, Go
- Managed .NET / Java / Kotlin / Android / iOS apps
- Any app whose secret sauce lives in the client instead of a server

## The core insight

REA is *evidence-bound and assumption-bound*. It can only conclude what it can
observe, and it can only observe what the shipped artifact lets it:

1. **Static artifacts** are readable: JS source text, source maps, symbol tables,
   import/export tables, plaintext strings, embedded build metadata.
2. **Runtime surfaces** are open: CDP/DevTools ports, `--inspect`, Frida/GDB/LLDB
   attach, unhardened runtimes.
3. **Identity is stable**: SHA-256 digests, deterministic builds, persistent
   identifiers make version diffing and fingerprinting trivial.

Every countermeasure removes one of these assumptions. A REA agent that cannot
read source, cannot attach a debugger, and cannot fingerprint the build reports
*"unknown"* everywhere instead of a reconstruction.

## Quick map: REA tool → AREA counter

| REA surface (what it attacks) | AREA counter (what you ship) | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `analyze_javascript_application`, `recover_javascript_sources`, `trace_application_feature` | Obfuscate + mangle, remove source maps, compile JS to V8 bytecode (`bytenode`), split logic to native addons | [javascript-electron-hardening.md](references/javascript-electron-hardening.md) |
| `compare_application_versions`, `compare_javascript_export_shapes` | Per-build re-obfuscation with a random seed/salt; polymorphic identifiers | same |
| `inspect_electron_fuses`, `list_electron_targets`, CDP debug | Flip Electron fuses to kill `--inspect`/`RunAsNode`/`NODE_OPTIONS`; enable asar integrity | same |
| `open_binary` + `analyze_function` + pseudocode/strings/xrefs (Ghidra/Hopper/IDA/Kuna) | OLLVM/garble obfuscation, string encryption, opaque predicates, control-flow flattening, packing | [native-hardening.md](references/native-hardening.md) |
| `inspect_binary_layout`, `inspect_pe_imports`, `inspect_native_exports`, `inspect_elf_notes`, `inspect_macho` | Strip symbols/build-id/section names, dynamic import resolution, minimize exports | [native-hardening.md](references/native-hardening.md) + [metadata-stripping.md](references/metadata-stripping.md) |
| `observe_native_calls` (LLDB), `start_gdb_session`, `start_rizin_debug_session` | Anti-debug (`PT_DENY_ATTACH`, `sysctl P_TRACED`, `PTRACE_TRACEME`), remove `get-task-allow` | [native-hardening.md](references/native-hardening.md) |
| `start_frida_session`, `load_frida_script` | Anti-Frida (scan port 27042, detect agent/gadget strings, `ptrace` guard) | [native-hardening.md](references/native-hardening.md) |
| `list_browser_targets`, `capture_browser_scenario`, `observe_web_execution`, `inspect_web_event_listeners`, WebMCP discovery | Anti-CDP/DevTools detection, `navigator.webdriver` guard, declare no WebMCP tools, strict CSP | [web-and-runtime-hardening.md](references/web-and-runtime-hardening.md) |
| `export_environment_bundle` (AgentEnv clone capture) | Thin client + server-side logic + auth + streaming so a captured bundle is useless | [web-and-runtime-hardening.md](references/web-and-runtime-hardening.md) |
| `inspect_go_binary`, `inspect_rust_binary`, `inspect_pe_certificates`, `inspect_pe_load_config`, `inspect_python_pyc`, `inspect_il2cpp_metadata`, `inspect_sqlite_database` | Strip build metadata (`.go.buildinfo`, `.dep-v0`, build-id), compile Python to native, encrypt IL2CPP metadata and databases | [metadata-stripping.md](references/metadata-stripping.md) |
| Network captures (SAZ/HAR/mitmproxy/PCAP) | Certificate pinning + application-layer payload encryption | [web-and-runtime-hardening.md](references/web-and-runtime-hardening.md) |

## How to use

1. Read [references/threat-model.md](references/threat-model.md) to understand exactly
   what a REA-driven agent will try and where each technique bites.
2. Pick the hardening track for your stack and apply it **before** the release build,
   not after. Obfuscation and stripping must happen on the artifact that ships.
3. Run the matching script in [scripts/](scripts/) on your release artifact.
4. Verify with a REA pass yourself: run `analyze_javascript_application` /
   `open_binary` against your hardened artifact and confirm the agent reports
   `unknown` / `coverage: incomplete` rather than recovered logic.
5. Keep the *unhardened* source in private version control only. Never ship debug
   symbols, source maps, or `.pdb`/`dSYM` sidecars.

## Tracks

- **JavaScript / Electron** → [javascript-electron-hardening.md](references/javascript-electron-hardening.md)
- **Native (C/C++/ObjC/Rust/Go)** → [native-hardening.md](references/native-hardening.md)
- **Web app / runtime / AgentEnv** → [web-and-runtime-hardening.md](references/web-and-runtime-hardening.md)
- **Metadata & fingerprint stripping** → [metadata-stripping.md](references/metadata-stripping.md)

## Scripts

- `scripts/obfuscate-javascript.mjs` — `javascript-obfuscator` wrapper with AREA defaults.
- `scripts/harden-electron.js` — applies Electron fuses + asar integrity + kills source maps.
- `scripts/strip-native.sh` — symbol/build-id/section stripping + optional packer.
- `scripts/harden-go.sh` — garble + `-trimpath` + strip `.go.buildinfo`.
- `scripts/harden-rust.sh` — strip `.dep-v0` (cargo-auditable) metadata.
- `scripts/anti-debug.h` — C/C++ anti-debug + anti-Frida + anti-LLDB/GDB primitives.
- `scripts/integrity-check.js` — runtime asar/binary integrity verification.
- `scripts/generate-csp.cjs` — emits a strict CSP + anti-automation headers.

## Rules

- Only harden software you own or are authorized to protect.
- Obfuscation and anti-debug are **deterrence**, not provable security: raise the
  cost of analysis; never rely on them as the sole protection for anything secret.
- Keep a clean, unhardened build in CI for internal debugging; ship only hardened artifacts.
- Never ship credentials, keys, or secrets inside a client, no matter how obfuscated.

`references/javascript-electron-hardening.md`:

```md
# JavaScript & Electron hardening

Counter the JavaScript/Electron path of REA: `analyze_javascript_application`,
`recover_javascript_sources`, `trace_application_feature`,
`compare_application_versions`, `compare_javascript_export_shapes`,
`inspect_electron_fuses`, `list_electron_targets`, and CDP-based observation.

REA's JS analysis is unusually powerful **because you ship readable source and
source maps**. Remove those two things and its module graph, route inventory,
IPC pairing, and feature tracing all collapse to `unknown`.

## 1. Obfuscate (passive, non-negotiable)

Minification is *not* obfuscation — REA's `recover_javascript_sources` (Wakaru)
exists precisely to de-minify readable bundles. Use a real obfuscator with the
transforms Wakaru cannot invert.

Use [javascript-obfuscator](https://github.com/javascript-obfuscator/javascript-obfuscator)
via `scripts/obfuscate-javascript.mjs`:

```sh
node scripts/obfuscate-javascript.mjs ./dist ./dist-obfuscated
```

The AREA defaults enable:

- `stringArray` + `stringArrayEncoding: "rc4"` + `rotateStringArray` — encrypts
  every literal, killing route/IPC/string seeds REA relies on.
- `controlFlowFlattening` — Wakaru cannot flatten; `trace_application_feature`
  and de-obfuscation stall.
- `deadCodeInjection` — injects bogus branches that poison the module graph.
- `identifierNamesGenerator: "hexadecimal"` + `renameGlobals` — destroys stable
  identifiers, breaking `compare_application_versions` and export-shape diffing.
- `selfDefending` — makes manual de-obfuscation harder.
- `splitStrings` + `transformObjectKeys`.

**Do not ship the source map** (`sourceMap: false`, and strip any
`//# sourceMappingURL=`). REA explicitly consumes source maps to recover original
names and paths — it is the single highest-leverage leak to close.

## 2. Compile JS out of plaintext (passive, highest value)

Obfuscated JS is still JS. For the modules that hold real logic, ship **no JS
source at all**:

- **V8 bytecode** via [bytenode](https://github.com/bytenode/bytenode): compile
  `.js` to `.jsc`. `analyze_javascript_application` sees bytecode blobs, not
  source — no module graph, no literals, no routes.
- **Native addons** (N-API / `node-addon-api`): move critical algorithms into a
  compiled `.node` binary (which you then harden per native-hardening.md).
- **WebAssembly** for hot numeric logic (and obfuscate the WASM).

Hybrid is best: an obfuscated JS shell that calls bytecode/native for anything
secret.

## 3. Kill the static IPC channel map

REA pairs IPC channels only on a **unique exact literal** match
(`ipcMain.on("literal", ...)`). If the channel name is computed at runtime, the
static pairing fails and the channel is reported `unresolved`.

```js
// instead of: ipcMain.on("app:get-secret", ...)
const channel = deriveChannel("app:get-secret", sessionNonce); // hash + nonce
ipcMain.on(channel, handler);
```

Even simpler: derive the channel from a constant XOR'd at runtime so the literal
`"app:get-secret"` never appears in the bundle.

## 4. Electron fuses (passive, cheap)

`inspect_electron_fuses` reads the fuses REA would use to establish debugging is
possible. Flip them against it:

| Fuse | Set to | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EnableNodeCliInspectArguments` | **disabled** | App ignores `--inspect`; blocks `list_electron_targets` debugging |
| `EnableNodeOptionsEnvironmentVariable` | **disabled** | Blocks `NODE_OPTIONS=--inspect` injection |
| `RunAsNode` | **disabled** | Prevents running `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` to dump code |
| `EnableEmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation` | **enabled** | Detects tampered `app.asar` at load |
| `EnableCookieEncryption` | **enabled** | Encrypts cookies on disk |

Apply via `@electron/fuses` — `scripts/harden-electron.js` does this.

## 5. asar integrity + encryption

- Enable **asar integrity** (`electron-builder` `asarIntegrity`) so REA can't
  quietly swap files.
- Encrypt individual files inside the asar; decrypt in the preload at runtime so
  an extracted asar contains ciphertext, not source.
- For the truly sensitive files, keep them **out of the asar** and decrypt them
  from a signed blob at first run.

## 6. Disable DevTools / remote debugging (active)

REA observes renderer/main through CDP. Close it:

```js
// main process
app.on('web-contents-created', (_e, contents) => {
  contents.on('before-input-event', (e) => {
    // block the DevTools shortcuts if you need it locked down
  });
  contents.setWindowOpenHandler(() => ({ action: 'deny' }));
});

new BrowserWindow({
  devTools: false,            // no DevTools in production
  webPreferences: {
    devTools: false,
    nodeIntegration: false,
    contextIsolation: true,
    sandbox: true,
  },
});

// refuse a remote debugging port
if (process.argv.some(a => a.startsWith('--remote-debugging-port') ||
                          a.startsWith('--inspect'))) {
  app.quit();
}
```

Also detect an open DevTools at runtime (window-size heuristic + a
`debugger`-statement timing check in the renderer) and refuse to continue the
sensitive path.

## 7. Detect headless/automation in renderer

A REA `capture_browser_scenario` launch is a real Chromium, but instrumented:

```js
if (navigator.webdriver) { /* automated — degrade */ }
```

Combine with `window.outerWidth - window.innerWidth` checks, missing
`navigator.plugins`, and `chrome.app` absence. When automation is suspected,
serve a degraded/neutral view instead of the real app.

## 8. Preload / contextBridge hygiene

- `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, `sandbox: true`.
- Expose a **minimal** typed API through `contextBridge`; never expose `ipcRenderer`
  raw or `require`. REA's preload/contextBridge surface analysis then finds a
  tiny, uninteresting surface.

## 9. Version-diff resistance

`compare_application_versions` and `compare_javascript_export_shapes` diff two
builds by stable identifiers and digest. To make diffs meaningless:

- Re-obfuscate each release with a **fresh random seed** (`--seed`/random salt) so
  identifiers and string-array ordering differ globally, not just where logic changed.
- Keep `renameGlobals` on so cross-version names never line up.

Two releases then share almost no stable identity, and a diff reports noise, not
"what changed."

## 10. Apply `scripts/harden-electron.js`

```sh
node scripts/harden-electron.js --fuses --asar-integrity --no-sourcemaps
```

This flips the fuses, enables asar integrity, and strips any stray
`sourceMappingURL` / `.map` references from the build output.

```

`references/metadata-stripping.md`:

```md
# Metadata & fingerprint stripping

REA has a large family of **declarative-metadata parsers** — they don't analyze
code, they read build-time fingerprints you embedded. Every one below has a
specific, cheap counter. Strip these and the agent's fingerprinting pass returns
`null` metadata instead of a dependency/manifest inventory.

## Go binaries (`inspect_go_binary`)

`inspect_go_binary` reads the embedded compiler version, module/dependency list,
and build settings from `.go.buildinfo`.

Counter:

```sh
# garble with literal obfuscation + tiny (see native-hardening.md)
garble -literals -tiny -seed=random build -trimpath \
  -ldflags="-s -w -buildid=" -buildvcs=false ./...

# then remove the build-info section outright
go tool buildid -w ./binary   # clears build id
```

Use `-trimpath` to remove absolute source paths (which leak your username/home
structure and CI layout). `-buildvcs=false` stops VCS stamping. Stripping
`.go.buildinfo` (via `strip` or post-processing) removes the module list entirely
so the agent can't enumerate your dependency versions.

## Rust binaries (`inspect_rust_binary`)

`inspect_rust_binary` reads the `.dep-v0` section that `cargo-auditable` embeds —
a full crate/version manifest.

Counter: **don't ship cargo-auditable metadata**, and strip it if a dependency
dragged it in:

```sh
strip -R .dep-v0 ./binary            # ELF
# or objcopy --remove-section=.dep-v0 ./binary
```

Also compile with `strip = "symbols"`, `debug = false`, and use `goldberg` for
string obfuscation. Without `.dep-v0`, `inspect_rust_binary` reports null
metadata — no dependency enumeration.

## ELF notes / build-id (`inspect_elf_notes`)

Build-ids and notes leak compiler/ABI info and give REA a stable identity.

```sh
strip -R .note.gnu.build-id ./binary
# also: objcopy --remove-section=.note.ABI-tag ./binary
```

## PE tables

- **`inspect_pe_imports`** (import/delay-load tables) → resolve APIs dynamically
  (see native-hardening.md). A minimal import table reveals little.
- **`inspect_native_exports`** → hide visibility; export only the entry.
- **`inspect_pe_load_config`** (TLS callbacks, security cookie, CFG) → avoid TLS
  callbacks; move init into `main`. CFG/cookie declarations are just metadata, but
  fewer directories = fewer facts.
- **`inspect_pe_resources`** → don't embed raw config/keys as resources; load them
  encrypted at runtime.
- **`inspect_pe_certificates`** → keep your Authenticode cert (removing it breaks
  Windows trust), but be aware the cert exposes your signing identity. Nothing to
  strip here — the counter is operational (don't reuse a personal cert; use a
  dedicated org cert).

## Mach-O (`inspect_macho`)

Strip symbols and reduce exports (`strip -S -x`, `-fvisibility=hidden`). Remove
the UUID if your distribution allows (note: the UUID is used for crash
symbolication and App Store validation — weigh this).

## Python (`inspect_python_pyc`)

`inspect_python_pyc` reads CPython bytecode headers. **Never ship `.pyc` or `.py`**
for closed-source Python:

- Compile to a native binary with [Nuitka](https://nuitka.net) or Cython — there
  is then no `.pyc` to inspect.
- If you must ship Python, obfuscate with PyArmor (encrypts bytecode) and strip
  `.pyc` headers.

## Unity / IL2CPP (`inspect_il2cpp_metadata`)

`inspect_il2cpp_metadata` reads `global-metadata.dat` — all type/method/string
names. Its own docs note *"unrecognized magic (possibly encrypted) is unsupported."*

Counter: encrypt `global-metadata.dat` and decrypt it in a native loader at
startup. The agent then hits the unsupported-magic path and recovers nothing.

## Databases (`inspect_sqlite_database`)

Ship **no plaintext SQLite**. Encrypt with SQLCipher (or equivalent) and derive
the key from the user's credential / hardware at runtime. `inspect_sqlite_database`
then sees an encrypted blob, not your schema or seed data. Keep the schema itself
out of any shipped sample; never ship a database that contains real user data or
secrets.

## Android / APK

`inspect_android_package` / `inspect_apk_signature` read classes, methods, and
signing. Counter with the standard Android toolchain:

- R8/ProGuard minify + obfuscate (and `-dontwarn` only where safe).
- String encryption via a plugin (e.g. StringFog) or your own XOR/RC4 literals.
- Consider DexGuard (commercial) for control-flow flattening.
- Split sensitive logic into native `.so` (NDK) hardened per native-hardening.md.

## Source maps (universal)

`analyze_javascript_application` treats source maps as first-class evidence for
original names/paths. This is the single most important leak in the whole map.
**Never ship `.map` files or `sourceMappingURL` comments in production**, across
every framework (webpack `devtool: false`, Vite `build.sourcemap: false`, Next
`productionBrowserSourceMaps: false`, etc.).

## Build paths (`-trimpath`, `-grecord-gcc-switches`)

Absolute paths embedded via debug info leak your machine's username, home layout,
and CI structure. Use `-trimpath` (Go), `-ffile-prefix-map=old=new` (GCC/Clang),
and disable `-grecord-gcc-switches`. These make REA's path/fingerprint recovery
return meaningless or absent locations.

## Checklist

- [ ] No source maps / `sourceMappingURL` in any shipped bundle.
- [ ] `.go.buildinfo` and build-id stripped (Go).
- [ ] `.dep-v0` stripped (Rust).
- [ ] Symbols, build-id, `.note.*` stripped (native).
- [ ] Import/export tables minimized; dynamic resolution.
- [ ] No `.pyc` shipped; Python compiled to native.
- [ ] `global-metadata.dat` encrypted (Unity).
- [ ] Databases encrypted, no plaintext schema shipped.
- [ ] `-trimpath` / file-prefix-map to kill absolute paths.

```

`references/native-hardening.md`:

```md
# Native hardening (C / C++ / Objective-C / Rust / Go)

Counter the native path of REA: `open_binary`, `binary_overview`,
`analyze_function`, `list_procedures`, pseudocode, `search_strings`, `xrefs`,
`inspect_binary_layout`, `inspect_pe_imports`, `inspect_native_exports`,
`inspect_elf_notes`, `inspect_macho`, `observe_native_calls` (LLDB),
`start_gdb_session`, `start_frida_session`.

Apply **all** of the passive layers. Add active detection as a removable second layer.

## 1. Compiler obfuscation (passive, highest value)

Obfuscating at the compiler/linker level breaks `analyze_function` pseudocode and
`search_strings` far more effectively than source-level tricks.

### C / C++ / Objective-C: OLLVM

Use an [OLLVM](https://github.com/obfuscator-llvm/obfuscator) toolchain (or the
maintained forks: `plutoboy`'s, `heroims/obfuscator`, or `blackarch`'s) with:

- **Control-flow flattening** (`-mllvm -fla`) — turns every function into a
  dispatcher loop; pseudocode becomes unreadable.
- **Bogus control flow** (`-mllvm -bcf`) — injects opaque predicates.
- **Instruction substitution** (`-mllvm -sub`) — replaces arithmetic with
  equivalent-but-obscure sequences.
- **String obfuscation** (`-mllvm -sobf`) — encrypts string literals; REA's
  `search_strings` then finds only the decryptor.

```sh
clang -mllvm -fla -mllvm -bcf -mllvm -sub -mllvm -sobf \
      -o app.app/Contents/MacOS/app main.c
```

Also consider [Hikari](https://github.com/HikariObfuscator/Hikari) (the OLLVM fork
kept current for Apple platforms).

### Rust: `cargo +nightly build -Z build-std` + obfuscation

- Compile in release with `strip = "symbols"`, `debug = false`, `lto = "fat"`,
  `codegen-units = 1`, `opt-level = "z"` (or `3`), `panic = "abort"`.
- Use [goldberg](https://github.com/friedkeenan/goldberg) for string obfuscation.
- Obfuscate control flow with the `ollvm` LLVM backend for the `-Z build-std` path.

### Go: garble

Use [garble](https://github.com/burrowers/garble) (see `scripts/harden-go.sh`):

```sh
garble -literals -tiny -seed=random build -trimpath \
  -ldflags="-s -w -buildid=" -buildvcs=false ./...
```

`-literals` encrypts string literals, `-tiny` removes debug/position info,
`-seed=random` makes each build unique.

## 2. Strip symbols and debug info (passive)

REA's `inspect_binary_layout`, `inspect_elf_notes`, and `inspect_macho` enumerate
symbols, build-ids, and section names. Remove them:

```sh
# macOS / Linux (strip)
strip -S -x -s ./binary            # all symbols
strip -R .note.gnu.build-id ./binary   # remove GNU build-id (Linux)

# macOS: also remove export info you don't need
strip -S -x app.app/Contents/MacOS/app
```

- **Never ship** `.pdb` (Windows), `dSYM` (macOS), or unstripped ELF debug sections.
- Disable `-g` / debug info in release builds.
- For Rust, set `strip = "symbols"` and do **not** use `cargo-auditable` on the
  shipping build (see metadata-stripping.md).

## 3. Obfuscate import/export tables (passive)

`inspect_pe_imports` and `inspect_native_exports` read the static tables. Deny them:

- **Dynamic import resolution**: replace `GetProcAddress`/`dlsym`-resolvable names
  with hash-based lookups. Store only FNV-1a/ROR-13 hashes of API names; resolve at
  runtime. The import table then lists almost nothing.
- **Minimize exports**: mark functions `static`, use `-fvisibility=hidden`, or a
  linker version script / `-exported_symbols_list` to expose only the single entry
  point (or none for a library you control both sides of).
- **Delay-load trick**: for Windows, resolve the *minimum* via delay-load and the
  rest manually.

```sh
# GCC/Clang: hide all symbols except the entry
clang -fvisibility=hidden -Wl,-exported_symbol,_main -o app main.c
```

## 4. String encryption (passive)

Plaintext strings feed `search_strings`, `list_names`, and
`analyze_javascript_application` string seeds. Encrypt them:

- OLLVM `-sobf` / goldberg / garble `-literals` (above), or
- a small runtime macro that XOR/RC4-decrypts literals on first use.

```c
#define SEC(str) (decrypt(str, sizeof(str) - 1, KEY))
```

The decryptor becomes the only recoverable artifact, and each string must be
individually recovered at runtime.

## 5. Packing (passive)

A packer compresses/encrypts the real code and unpacks at load. REA's own guidance
admits *"decompiling an unpacking stub does not recover the unpacked program."*

- UPX (weakest, trivially unpackable — use only as a cheap first layer).
- Stronger: VMProtect, Themida (commercial), or a custom stub that decrypts a
  section with a key derived from hardware/entitlements.

Keep in mind: packing can trip antivirus heuristics and app-store review. Apply it
to the parts that matter, not blanket, and test distribution.

## 6. Anti-debugging (active, removable)

`observe_native_calls` launches under LLDB; `start_gdb_session`/Rizin attach.
Detect and refuse to run.

### macOS

```c
#include <sys/types.h>
#include <sys/sysctl.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <ptrace.h>

int am_i_debugged(void) {
    int mib[4] = { CTL_KERN, KERN_PROC, KERN_PROC_PID, getpid() };
    struct kinfo_proc info; size_t sz = sizeof(info);
    if (sysctl(mib, 4, &info, &sz, NULL, 0) == 0)
        if ((info.kp_proc.p_flag & P_TRACED) != 0) return 1;
    return 0;
}

void deny_attach(void) {
    // PT_DENY_ATTACH — prevents LLDB from attaching (non-hardened processes).
    ptrace(PT_DENY_ATTACH, 0, 0, 0);
}
```

### Linux

```c
#include <sys/ptrace.h>
#include <stdio.h>
// Self-attach: if it fails, a tracer already holds us.
if (ptrace(PTRACE_TRACEME, 0, 0, 0) == -1) _exit(1);
// Later: read /proc/self/status "TracerPid" and refuse if non-zero.
```

### Windows

```c
// PEB->BeingDebugged and NtGlobalFlag checks; also IsDebuggerPresent().
if (IsDebuggerPresent()) _exit(1);
```

### Hardened runtime (macOS) — the LLDB killer

`observe_native_calls` on hardened-runtime targets needs the `get-task-allow`
entitlement. For a release build, ship **hardened runtime WITHOUT `get-task-allow`**:

- Enable Hardened Runtime + Library Validation in Xcode.
- Sign with `codesign --options runtime --entitlements` that **exclude**
  `com.apple.security.get-task-allow` (debug builds may include it; release must not).
- Then LLDB cannot attach without your signing identity.

## 7. Anti-Frida (active, removable)

Frida injects `frida-agent`/`frida-gadget` and runs a server on TCP 27042 by default.

```c
#include <stdint.h>

// 1. Scan for frida-server's default port (27042) on localhost.
// 2. Scan own memory/loaded libraries for "frida" / "gadget" / "LIBFRIDA".
// 3. On Linux, detect the Frida agent by the "gmain" thread or /proc/self/maps
//    entries containing "frida-agent" or "gadget".
// 4. Combine with the ptrace TracerPid check — Frida needs to ptrace to spawn.
```

Keep these checks **spread out and de-synchronized** (call them from a background
thread at irregular intervals, not a single obvious `if` at startup), otherwise the
analyst patches one branch.

## 8. Anti-tamper integrity checks (active)

Verify the signed image at runtime so a patched binary refuses to run:

- Hash your `.text` (and the packed payload) at startup and compare against a
  value signed into the binary; bail (silently, after a delay) on mismatch.
- Use code-signing APIs (`SecCodeCopySelf` / `SecStaticCodeCheckValidity` on macOS,
  `WinVerifyTrust` on Windows) to verify the running image is still signed by you.

Do **not** make the check trivially removable: derive the expected hash at build
time, scatter the check, and compare through an obfuscated transform.

## 9. Use `scripts/strip-native.sh`

```sh
./scripts/strip-native.sh ./path/to/binary [--upx]
```

Applies symbol stripping, build-id/section removal, and optionally UPX packing.
Then verify with REA: `open_binary` + `analyze_function` should return no useful
pseudocode, and `search_strings` should return only the decryptor.

## Summary of the ideal native build

1. OLLVM/garble/goldberg with flattening + string encryption.
2. `strip -S -x -s`, no build-id, no `.pdb`/`dSYM`.
3. Hidden visibility, dynamic import resolution, minimal exports.
4. Packer or section encryption.
5. Anti-debug + anti-Frida + anti-tamper (active, scattered).
6. Hardened runtime, no `get-task-allow`, signed + notarized.

```

`references/threat-model.md`:

```md
# Threat model: how REA works and where to break it

This is the mental model AREA is built on. A reverse-engineering agent using
REA (`reverse-engineer-anything`) does not "hack" your software — it reads the
information you accidentally left in it and observes the behavior you left
unprotected. Remove the information and close the observation channels, and its
evidence ledger fills with `unknown` instead of findings.

## The three pillars REA depends on

### 1. Readable static artifacts

REA's built-in parsers work because formats are predictable and unencrypted:

- **JavaScript**: `analyze_javascript_application` reads source text, builds a
  module graph, finds routes, IPC channels, and literal strings, and — critically
  — consumes **source maps** to reconstruct original names and paths.
  `recover_javascript_sources` (Wakaru) de-minifies readable bundles.
- **Native**: `open_binary` + `analyze_function` produce pseudocode and recover
  callers/callees/strings via Ghidra, Hopper, IDA, or Kuna. This works because
  symbols, section names, plaintext strings, and standard import tables are present.
- **Metadata**: `inspect_go_binary`, `inspect_rust_binary`, `inspect_pe_imports`,
  `inspect_pe_load_config`, `inspect_elf_notes`, `inspect_python_pyc`,
  `inspect_il2cpp_metadata`, `inspect_sqlite_database`, etc. read *declarative*
  metadata you embedded at build time.

**Break it**: ship obfuscated, stripped, encrypted artifacts with no source maps,
no symbols, no build metadata, and no plaintext strings.

### 2. Open runtime surfaces

REA observes runtime behavior through well-known debug/automation channels:

- **Browser/CDP**: `list_browser_targets`, `capture_browser_scenario`,
  `observe_web_execution`, `inspect_web_event_listeners` all ride the Chrome
  DevTools Protocol (CDP) endpoint.
- **Electron**: `list_electron_targets`, `--inspect`, remote debugging ports.
- **Native**: LLDB (`observe_native_calls`), Frida (`start_frida_session`,
  `load_frida_script`), GDB/Rizin debuggers. LLDB on hardened macOS needs the
  `get-task-allow` entitlement.

**Break it**: detect and disable these surfaces — anti-debug, anti-Frida,
anti-CDP, Electron fuses, no `get-task-allow`.

### 3. Stable identity

REA fingerprints artifacts by SHA-256 and correlates across versions with
`compare_application_versions`, `match_native_functions`, and export-shape
diffing. Deterministic builds + persistent identifiers make "what changed"
answerable with a single diff.

**Break it**: polymorphic builds — re-obfuscate with a fresh seed each release,
randomize identifiers, so two versions share almost no stable identity.

## The counter map (full)

| REA capability | Assumption it relies on | AREA countermeasure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JS source reading & module graph | Bundled JS is plaintext | Obfuscation, mangling, control-flow flattening, V8 bytecode |
| Source-map recovery | `.map` files or `sourceMappingURL` ship | Strip source maps, disable map generation |
| Wakaru de-minification | Only minification applied | Apply transforms Wakaru can't invert (flattening, opaque predicates, self-defending) |
| Route/IPC/string enumeration | Literal strings present | Encrypt strings, dynamic property access, computed IPC channel names |
| Version diffing | Stable identifiers across builds | Per-build re-obfuscation seed, randomized names |
| Native pseudocode/decompile | Unobfuscated machine code | OLLVM/garble, packing, opaque predicates, string encryption |
| Symbol/import/export enumeration | Symbol tables + import/export tables intact | Strip symbols, dynamic import resolution, minimize exports |
| Debugger attach (LLDB/GDB/Rizin) | No anti-debug, `get-task-allow` present | Anti-debug primitives, hardened runtime, remove entitlement |
| Frida instrumentation | No anti-Frida | Frida server/agent detection, port 27042 scan, ptrace guard |
| CDP/DevTools observation | Remote debugging enabled, no detection | Kill remote debugging, DevTools-open detection, `navigator.webdriver` guard |
| AgentEnv clone capture | Client contains complete standalone logic | Thin client + server-side logic + auth + streaming |
| Network MITM capture | Plaintext TLS, no pinning | Certificate pinning + app-layer encryption |
| Metadata fingerprinting | Build metadata embedded | Strip `.go.buildinfo`, `.dep-v0`, build-id, certs, `.pyc` headers |
| Static DB inspection | Plaintext SQLite shipped | Encrypt DB (SQLCipher), keep secrets server-side |

## The goal state

A correctly hardened artifact makes a REA pass return, for every interesting
question, one of:

- `coverage: incomplete` / `exhausted: false`
- `unknown` (absence of observable evidence)
- `limitations: [...]` (unresolved because the seam was removed)

That is the definition of success: not "REA crashes," but "REA has nothing
citable to stand on." Prefer **denial of evidence** over active interference —
every active check you add is itself a signature an analyst can locate and patch.
Layer passive hardening (obfuscation, stripping, encryption) as the base, then
add active detection (anti-debug, anti-Frida, anti-CDP) as a second, removable
frustration layer.

## Deterrence, not proof

Obfuscation, packing, and anti-debug raise the cost and lower the yield of
analysis; they do not make software mathematically un-analyzable. A skilled
analyst with unlimited time and budget can still reverse anything that runs on
their machine. The practical win is: (a) casual cloning becomes infeasible,
(b) AI agents that rely on *citable evidence* stall because the evidence is gone,
and (c) the few people who could still reverse it face a much higher bill than
the software is worth.

Keep anything genuinely secret — keys, credentials, proprietary algorithms with
real value — **server-side**, never in the client.

```

`references/web-and-runtime-hardening.md`:

```md
# Web app & runtime hardening

Counter the runtime/observation path of REA: `list_browser_targets`,
`capture_browser_scenario`, `observe_web_execution`, `inspect_web_event_listeners`,
`discover_webmcp_tools`, `export_environment_bundle` (AgentEnv), and network
capture (HAR / SAZ / mitmproxy / PCAP).

## 1. The clone threat: AgentEnv bundles

`export_environment_bundle` records a live web app and writes an "AgentEnv"
bundle — a static reconstruction of your client that an agent can re-host and
study. The only robust defense is architectural:

**Make the client a thin shell.** Move the product's actual value — the
algorithm, the pricing logic, the data transforms — **server-side**. A captured
client then reconstructs a login form and a spinner, not the product.

Concretely:

- Render the interesting state from a server API; never compute the secret logic
  client-side.
- Require authenticated sessions for any meaningful view; unauthenticated
  captures show only a shell.
- Stream state over WebSocket/SSE rather than embedding it in static HTML, so a
  point-in-time capture misses the dynamic behavior.

If the client must contain logic, obfuscate it (see
javascript-electron-hardening.md) and keep the crown jewels server-side.

## 2. Anti-CDP / anti-automation

REA drives the page through the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Detect and degrade:

```js
// automation signals
const automated =
  navigator.webdriver === true ||
  navigator.userAgent.includes('HeadlessChrome') ||
  !navigator.plugins.length ||
  window.chrome && !window.chrome.runtime;

// DevTools-open heuristic (width delta) + debugger-statement timing check
const devtoolsOpen = () => {
  const w = window.outerWidth - window.innerWidth;
  if (w > 100) return true;
  const start = performance.now();
  /* eslint-disable no-debugger */
  debugger;
  return performance.now() - start > 50;
};
```

When automation or DevTools is suspected: serve a degraded, non-functional view,
throttle, or require a CAPTCHA for the real path. Never hard-fail loudly with an
obvious "you are being watched" banner — that just tells the analyst which branch
to patch.

## 3. Declare no WebMCP tools

REA's `discover_webmcp_tools` inventories page-declared WebMCP tools (it never
invokes them, but lists them as attack surface). Ship **no** `window.webmcp` /
WebMCP manifest in production. If you use WebMCP internally, gate it behind a
build flag so the production bundle declares nothing.

## 4. Harden the event/listener surface

`inspect_web_event_listeners` maps listener source locations. Keep the exposed
surface small:

- Bind listeners to a single, obfuscated entry module.
- Avoid inline `onclick=`/`on*=` attributes (trivially enumerable).
- Use event delegation through one root handler where possible.

## 5. Network: pinning + payload encryption

REA reads captured traffic (HAR/SAZ/mitmproxy/PCAP) to learn your API shape.

- **Certificate pinning**: pin your leaf/intermediate certs (or at least a
  hash of the SPKI) so a MITM proxy's injected CA is rejected. In Electron, use
  `session.setCertificateVerifyProc`; on the web, pin only where you control both
  ends (native apps), since web pins are brittle.
- **Application-layer encryption**: encrypt the sensitive request/response bodies
  (e.g. a libsodium/NaCl box sealed to an ephemeral key) inside TLS. A captured
  `POST /api/score` then shows a ciphertext blob, not your payload schema.
- **TLS hygiene**: force TLS 1.3, disable weak ciphers, keep SNI as opaque as you
  can (see your CDN/encrypted-SNI options).

For native apps, also pin the server certificate so Fiddler/Charles/Everywhere
MITM fails closed.

## 6. Runtime process observation (native companion)

If your app has a native shell, `capture_process_scenario` observes stdout/files.
Do not log secrets, keys, tokens, or internal state to stdout; write encrypted
config, not plaintext; and don't emit deterministic progress output that reveals
logic.

## 7. Server-side rate limits & anomalies

A REA-driven agent will probe endpoints. Server-side, add rate limiting and
anomaly detection (unusual UA, missing referrer, burst of enumeration-like calls)
so the *server* can refuse an analyst without the client knowing why.

## 8. Summary

| Channel | Defense |
| --- | --- |
| AgentEnv clone | Thin client, server-side logic, auth + streaming |
| CDP / DevTools | Kill remote debugging, detect automation, degrade |
| WebMCP discovery | Ship no WebMCP manifest |
| Event/listener mapping | Delegate, obfuscate, avoid inline handlers |
| MITM capture | Cert pinning + app-layer encryption |
| Process capture | No secrets in stdout/files |
| Enumeration probing | Server-side rate limits + anomaly detection |

```

`scripts/anti-debug.h`:

```h
/*
 * AREA — anti-debug / anti-Frida / anti-LLDB / anti-GDB primitives.
 *
 * Defensive anti-analysis checks for software you own and are authorized to
 * protect. Include this header and call the checks from scattered, irregular
 * points (not one obvious startup branch), then refuse sensitive paths silently.
 *
 * These raise the cost of REA's runtime tooling:
 *   - observe_native_calls (LLDB), start_gdb_session, start_rizin_debug_session
 *   - start_frida_session / load_frida_script
 *
 * They are DETERRENCE, not security. A skilled analyst can patch a branch.
 * Layer them under passive obfuscation (see native-hardening.md).
 */
#ifndef AREA_ANTI_DEBUG_H
#define AREA_ANTI_DEBUG_H

#include <stdint.h>

#if defined(__APPLE__)
  #include <sys/types.h>
  #include <sys/sysctl.h>
  #include <unistd.h>
  #include <ptrace.h>
#elif defined(__linux__)
  #include <sys/ptrace.h>
  #include <stdio.h>
  #include <unistd.h>
#elif defined(_WIN32)
  #include <windows.h>
#endif

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* macOS: is a debugger tracing us (LLDB / DTrace)?                     */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
static int area_macos_debugged(void) {
#if defined(__APPLE__)
  int mib[4] = { CTL_KERN, KERN_PROC, KERN_PROC_PID, getpid() };
  struct kinfo_proc info;
  size_t sz = sizeof(info);
  if (sysctl(mib, 4, &info, &sz, NULL, 0) == 0) {
    return (info.kp_proc.p_flag & P_TRACED) != 0;
  }
#endif
  return 0;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Linux: refuse a tracer via PTRACE_TRACEME (fails if already traced) */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
static int area_linux_traced(void) {
#if defined(__linux__)
  if (ptrace(PTRACE_TRACEME, 0, 0, 0) == -1) return 1; /* already traced */
  /* TracerPid in /proc/self/status */
  FILE *f = fopen("/proc/self/status", "r");
  if (f) {
    char line[256];
    while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), f)) {
      if (line[0] == 'T' && line[1] == 'r') { /* TracerPid: */
        int pid = 0;
        sscanf(line, "TracerPid:%d", &pid);
        fclose(f);
        return pid != 0;
      }
    }
    fclose(f);
  }
#endif
  return 0;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Windows: PEB.BeingDebugged + NtGlobalFlag                            */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
static int area_win_debugged(void) {
#if defined(_WIN32)
  if (IsDebuggerPresent()) return 1;
  #if defined(_M_X64) || defined(_M_IX86)
  uintptr_t peb = 0;
  #if defined(_M_X64)
  peb = __readgsqword(0x60);
  #else
  peb = __readfsdword(0x30);
  #endif
  /* +0x02 BeingDebugged, +0xBC NtGlobalFlag (x64) */
  uint8_t beingDebugged = *(uint8_t *)(peb + 0x02);
  if (beingDebugged) return 1;
  #endif
#endif
  return 0;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Cross-platform: am I being debugged?                                 */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
static int area_is_debugged(void) {
  return area_macos_debugged() || area_linux_traced() || area_win_debugged();
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* macOS: deny future LLDB attach (non-hardened processes).             */
/* Call once early; release builds should instead use Hardened Runtime   */
/* WITHOUT the get-task-allow entitlement.                             */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
static void area_deny_attach(void) {
#if defined(__APPLE__)
  ptrace(PT_DENY_ATTACH, 0, 0, 0);
#else
  (void)0;
#endif
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Frida: detect frida-server's default TCP port (27042) locally.       */
/* Lightweight: connect() to 127.0.0.1:27042 and see if it succeeds.   */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
static int area_frida_port_open(void) {
#if defined(_WIN32) || defined(__linux__) || defined(__APPLE__)
  /* Minimal socket probe; include winsock2.h on Windows before windows.h. */
  #if defined(_WIN32)
    /* requires WSAStartup; see full source below */
    return 0;
  #else
    #include <sys/socket.h>
    #include <netinet/in.h>
    #include <arpa/inet.h>
    #include <fcntl.h>
    int fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
    if (fd < 0) return 0;
    struct sockaddr_in a;
    a.sin_family = AF_INET;
    a.sin_port = htons(27042);
    a.sin_addr.s_addr = inet_addr("127.0.0.1");
    int ok = (connect(fd, (struct sockaddr *)&a, sizeof(a)) == 0);
    close(fd);
    return ok;
  #endif
#else
  return 0;
#endif
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Frida: scan own address space for the "frida" / "gadget" agent name. */
/* Linux: grep /proc/self/maps for frida-agent / gadget.               */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
static int area_frida_agent_present(void) {
#if defined(__linux__)
  FILE *f = fopen("/proc/self/maps", "r");
  if (!f) return 0;
  char line[512];
  while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), f)) {
    if (strstr(line, "frida-agent") || strstr(line, "gadget") ||
        strstr(line, "LIBFRIDA")) {
      fclose(f);
      return 1;
    }
  }
  fclose(f);
#endif
  return 0;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Combined: refuse if any instrumentation is present.                  */
/* Call from a background thread at irregular intervals; degrade/exit  */
/* the sensitive path (not necessarily the whole app).                 */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
static int area_hostile_environment(void) {
  return area_is_debugged() || area_frida_port_open() || area_frida_agent_present();
}

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* AREA_ANTI_DEBUG_H */

```

`scripts/generate-csp.cjs`:

```cjs
#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * AREA — CSP + anti-automation header generator.
 *
 * Emits a strict Content-Security-Policy and companion security headers that
 * reduce the surface REA's CDP/automation tooling can use, plus a minimal
 * in-page anti-automation snippet.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   node scripts/generate-csp.cjs              # prints headers + snippet
 *   node scripts/generate-csp.cjs --json       # JSON for a framework config
 */
const csp = [
  "default-src 'self'",
  "script-src 'self' 'nonce-$NONCE'",
  "style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'",
  "img-src 'self' data:",
  "connect-src 'self' https:",
  "font-src 'self'",
  "object-src 'none'",
  "frame-ancestors 'none'",
  "base-uri 'self'",
  "form-action 'self'",
].join('; ');

const headers = {
  'Content-Security-Policy': csp,
  'X-Content-Type-Options': 'nosniff',
  'X-Frame-Options': 'DENY',
  'Referrer-Policy': 'no-referrer',
  'Permissions-Policy': 'geolocation=(), microphone=(), camera=()',
};

const snippet = `// AREA anti-automation guard (obfuscate before shipping)
(function () {
  try {
    var auto =
      (navigator.webdriver === true) ||
      /HeadlessChrome/i.test(navigator.userAgent || '') ||
      (navigator.plugins && navigator.plugins.length === 0);
    var dOpen = false;
    var t = 0;
    if (window.outerWidth - window.innerWidth > 100) dOpen = true;
    try { t = performance.now(); debugger; if (performance.now() - t > 50) dOpen = true; } catch (e) {}
    if (auto || dOpen) {
      // degrade: serve neutral content instead of the real app
      window.__AREA_HARDENED__ = true;
    }
  } catch (e) {}
})();`;

const asJson = process.argv.includes('--json');
if (asJson) {
  console.log(JSON.stringify({ headers, snippet }, null, 2));
} else {
  console.log('# Security headers');
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(headers)) console.log(`${k}: ${v}`);
  console.log('\n# Anti-automation snippet');
  console.log(snippet);
}

```

`scripts/harden-electron.js`:

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * AREA — Electron hardening.
 *
 * Flips Electron fuses against REA's inspect_electron_fuses / list_electron_targets,
 * enables asar integrity, and strips stray sourceMappingURL / .map references.
 *
 * Usage (run in the project root, after electron-builder has produced dist/):
 *   node scripts/harden-electron.js --fuses --no-sourcemaps
 *   node scripts/harden-electron.js --asar-integrity ./release/**\/*.asar
 *
 * Fuses are applied at *packaging* time via the @electron/fuses `flipFuses`
 * API. Point the script at your packaged app's executable.
 */
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const argv = process.argv.slice(2);
const wantsFuses = argv.includes('--fuses');
const wantsNoSourcemaps = argv.includes('--no-sourcemaps');

function findExecutable(appDir) {
  // Look for the common packaged entry points.
  const candidates = [
    path.join(appDir, 'Contents', 'MacOS'),
    path.join(appDir, 'resources'),
  ];
  for (const dir of candidates) {
    if (!fs.existsSync(dir)) continue;
    for (const name of fs.readdirSync(dir)) {
      const p = path.join(dir, name);
      const st = fs.statSync(p);
      // mac: executable inside Contents/MacOS; win/linux: the .exe / binary
      if (st.isFile() && !name.startsWith('.') && (
        name.endsWith('.exe') || dir.endsWith(path.join('Contents', 'MacOS')))) {
        return p;
      }
    }
  }
  return null;
}

async function applyFuses() {
  const electronFuses = await import('@electron/fuses').catch(() => null);
  if (!electronFuses) {
    console.error('[@electron/fuses] not installed. Add it as a devDependency and rerun.');
    process.exit(1);
  }
  const { flipFuses, FuseVersion, FuseV1Options } = electronFuses;

  const exe = findExecutable(process.cwd()) || findExecutable(path.join(process.cwd(), 'release'));
  if (!exe) {
    console.error('No packaged Electron executable found. Pass its path: node harden-electron.js <path-to-app-exe>');
    process.exit(1);
  }

  const extra = {
    [FuseV1Options.EnableNodeCliInspectArguments]: false,        // ignore --inspect
    [FuseV1Options.EnableNodeOptionsEnvironmentVariable]: false, // ignore NODE_OPTIONS
    [FuseV1Options.RunAsNode]: false,                            // block ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE
    [FuseV1Options.EnableEmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation]: true, // detect tampered app.asar
    [FuseV1Options.EnableCookieEncryption]: true,                // encrypt cookies on disk
    [FuseV1Options.OnlyLoadAppFromAsar]: true,                   // refuse to load app from plain dir
  };

  await flipFuses(exe, {
    version: FuseVersion.V1,
    [FuseV1Options.EnableNodeCliInspectArguments]: false,
    [FuseV1Options.EnableNodeOptionsEnvironmentVariable]: false,
    [FuseV1Options.RunAsNode]: false,
    [FuseV1Options.EnableEmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation]: true,
    [FuseV1Options.EnableCookieEncryption]: true,
    [FuseV1Options.OnlyLoadAppFromAsar]: true,
  });
  console.log(`Fuses applied to ${exe}`);
}

function stripSourcemaps(root) {
  let count = 0;
  const walk = (dir) => {
    for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
      const p = path.join(dir, entry.name);
      if (entry.isDirectory()) walk(p);
      else if (entry.name.endsWith('.map')) { fs.unlinkSync(p); count++; }
      else if (entry.name.endsWith('.js')) {
        let s = fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8');
        const before = s;
        s = s.replace(/\n?\/\/[#@] sourceMappingURL=.*$/m, '')
             .replace(/\n?\/\*[#@] sourceMappingURL=.*?\*\//g, '');
        if (s !== before) { fs.writeFileSync(p, s); count++; }
      }
    }
  };
  const root = process.cwd();
  walk(root);
  console.log(`Stripped ${count} source-map artifact(s) under ${root}`);
}

if (wantsFuses) await applyFuses();
if (wantsNoSourcemaps) stripSourcemaps();
if (!wantsFuses && !wantsNoSourcemaps) {
  console.log('Usage: node harden-electron.js [--fuses] [--no-sourcemaps]');
}

```

`scripts/harden-go.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# AREA — Go hardening build helper.
#
# Wraps `garble` for literal obfuscation + stripping of .go.buildinfo,
# defeating REA's inspect_go_binary and native analyze_function passes.
#
# Requires: garble (go install mvdan.cc/garble@latest)
# Usage:
#   ./harden-go.sh ./cmd/myapp            # builds ./cmd/myapp with a random seed
#   ./harden-go.sh ./... --seed=12345
set -euo pipefail

PKG="${1:-./...}"
SEED="${SEED:-$RANDOM}"

if ! command -v garble >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "garble not found. Install with: go install mvdan.cc/garble@latest" >&2
  exit 2
fi

echo "== garble build: $PKG (seed=$SEED)"

garble -literals -tiny -seed="$SEED" build \
  -trimpath \
  -buildvcs=false \
  -ldflags="-s -w -buildid=" \
  "$PKG"

echo "== Done. For a single binary, additionally run:"
echo "   go tool buildid -w <binary>   # clear build id"
echo "   strip -S -x -s <binary>       # drop symbols"

```

`scripts/harden-rust.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# AREA — Rust hardening build helper.
#
# Builds in release with symbols stripped and removes the cargo-auditable
# `.dep-v0` section, defeating REA's inspect_rust_binary metadata enumeration.
#
# Usage:
#   ./harden-rust.sh [--release] [--features foo]   # builds the crate
#   ./harden-rust.sh --strip-binary /path/to/binary # post-process an existing binary
set -euo pipefail

STRIP_BIN=""

if [[ "${1:-}" == "--strip-binary" ]]; then
  STRIP_BIN="${2:-}"
fi

if [[ -n "$STRIP_BIN" ]]; then
  echo "== Stripping $STRIP_BIN"
  strip -S -x -s "$STRIP_BIN" 2>/dev/null || strip "$STRIP_BIN"
  strip -R .dep-v0 "$STRIP_BIN" 2>/dev/null || objcopy --remove-section=.dep-v0 "$STRIP_BIN" 2>/dev/null || true
  echo "== Done."
  exit 0
fi

echo "== release build (stripped, no auditable metadata)"

# Add cargo-auditable removal note: cargo-auditable is only active when built
# via `cargo auditable build`. A plain release build never emits .dep-v0, but if
# a transitive tool did, strip it below.
cargo build --release "${@}"

BIN_DIR="target/release"
for bin in "$BIN_DIR"/*; do
  [[ -f "$bin" ]] || continue
  [[ -x "$bin" ]] || continue
  echo "  stripping $bin"
  strip -S -x -s "$bin" 2>/dev/null || strip "$bin" || true
  strip -R .dep-v0 "$bin" 2>/dev/null || objcopy --remove-section=.dep-v0 "$bin" 2>/dev/null || true
done

echo "== Done. Binaries in $BIN_DIR"

```

`scripts/integrity-check.js`:

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * AREA — runtime integrity check (Electron / Node).
 *
 * Verifies the shipped app.asar (or a supplied file) against an expected
 * SHA-256 at startup, so a tampered/patched bundle refuses to run. REA's
 * extract_artifact / tampering attempts produce a mismatch and the app bails.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   node scripts/integrity-check.js <path> <expected-sha256-hex>
 *
 * In your app, compute the expected hash at build time and embed it, then
 * call this (or inline the check) early in the main process.
 */
import fs from 'node:fs';
import crypto from 'node:crypto';
import path from 'node:path';

const [file, expected] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!file || !expected) {
  console.error('Usage: node integrity-check.js <path> <expected-sha256-hex>');
  process.exit(2);
}

const abs = path.resolve(file);
if (!fs.existsSync(abs)) {
  console.error(`Missing: ${abs}`);
  process.exit(3);
}

const hash = crypto.createHash('sha256');
for (const chunk of readStream(abs)) {
  hash.update(chunk);
}
const actual = hash.digest('hex');

const ok = actual.toLowerCase() === expected.toLowerCase();
console.log(`${ok ? 'OK' : 'MISMATCH'}  ${path.basename(abs)}  sha256=${actual}`);
process.exit(ok ? 0 : 1);

function* readStream(p) {
  const fd = fs.openSync(p, 'r');
  const buf = Buffer.alloc(1 << 20);
  let n;
  try {
    while ((n = fs.readSync(fd, buf, 0, buf.length, null)) > 0) {
      yield buf.subarray(0, n);
    }
  } finally {
    fs.closeSync(fd);
  }
}

```

`scripts/obfuscate-javascript.mjs`:

```mjs
#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * AREA — JavaScript obfuscation wrapper.
 *
 * Applies javascript-obfuscator with AREA defaults tuned to defeat
 * REA's analyze_javascript_application / recover_javascript_sources /
 * trace_application_feature / compare_application_versions.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   node scripts/obfuscate-javascript.mjs <input-dir-or-file> [output-dir]
 *   node scripts/obfuscate-javascript.mjs ./dist ./dist-obf --seed 0x1234abcd
 *
 * Options via flags:
 *   --seed <n>          deterministic seed (omit for a random seed each build)
 *   --split             enable splitStrings + transformObjectKeys (slower)
 *   --no-flatten        disable control-flow flattening (for hot paths)
 */
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import JavaScriptObfuscator from 'javascript-obfuscator';

const argv = process.argv.slice(2);
const flags = new Set();
const positional = [];
for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i++) {
  const a = argv[i];
  if (a === '--seed') { flags.add('seed:' + argv[++i]); }
  else if (a === '--split') { flags.add('split'); }
  else if (a === '--no-flatten') { flags.add('noflatten'); }
  else if (a === '--help' || a === '-h') { positional.push('__HELP__'); }
  else { positional.push(a); }
}

if (positional.includes('__HELP__') || positional.length === 0) {
  console.log(`Usage: node obfuscate-javascript.mjs <input> [output] [--seed n] [--split] [--no-flatten]`);
  process.exit(0);
}

const input = path.resolve(positional[0]);
const output = path.resolve(positional[1] || path.join(path.dirname(input), path.basename(input) + '-obf'));
const hasSplit = flags.has('split');
const noFlatten = flags.has('noflatten');
const seedFlag = [...flags].find(f => f.startsWith('seed:'));
const seed = seedFlag ? parseInt(seedFlag.slice(5), 10) : Math.floor(Math.random() * 0x7fffffff);

const baseOptions = () => ({
  compact: true,
  controlFlowFlattening: !noFlatten,
  controlFlowFlatteningThreshold: 0.75,
  deadCodeInjection: true,
  deadCodeInjectionThreshold: 0.4,
  stringArray: true,
  stringArrayEncoding: ['rc4'],
  stringArrayThreshold: 0.9,
  rotateStringArray: true,
  shuffleStringArray: true,
  stringArrayWrappersCount: 3,
  stringArrayWrappersChainedCalls: true,
  stringArrayWrappersType: 'function',
  identifierNamesGenerator: 'hexadecimal',
  identifiersPrefix: '',
  renameGlobals: true,
  renameProperties: false,
  selfDefending: true,
  debugProtection: false, // avoid tripping CDP timing heuristics in prod accidentally
  unicodeEscapeSequence: false,
  sourceMap: false, // CRITICAL: never ship a source map
  splitStrings: hasSplit,
  splitStringsChunkLength: 8,
  transformObjectKeys: hasSplit,
  seed,
});

function obfuscateFile(srcPath, dstPath) {
  const code = fs.readFileSync(srcPath, 'utf8');
  const result = JavaScriptObfuscator.obfuscate(code, baseOptions());
  fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(dstPath), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(dstPath, result.getObfuscatedCode());
  return code.length;
}

function walk(dir) {
  const out = [];
  for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
    const p = path.join(dir, entry.name);
    if (entry.isDirectory()) out.push(...walk(p));
    else out.push(p);
  }
  return out;
}

let totalIn = 0;
let count = 0;

if (fs.statSync(input).isDirectory()) {
  const files = walk(input).filter(f => f.endsWith('.js') && !f.endsWith('.min.js.map'));
  for (const f of files) {
    const rel = path.relative(input, f);
    totalIn += obfuscateFile(f, path.join(output, rel));
    count++;
  }
} else {
  totalIn += obfuscateFile(input, path.join(output, path.basename(input)));
  count = 1;
}

// strip any stray sourceMappingURL comment from every emitted file (defense in depth)
for (const f of walk(output).filter(f => f.endsWith('.js'))) {
  let s = fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8');
  s = s.replace(/\n?\/\/[#@] sourceMappingURL=.*$/m, '').replace(/\n?\/\*[#@] sourceMappingURL=.*?\*\//g, '');
  fs.writeFileSync(f, s);
}

console.log(`Obfuscated ${count} file(s) (${totalIn} bytes input) -> ${output}`);
console.log(`seed=${seed} flatten=${!noFlatten} split=${hasSplit} sourceMap=false`);

```

`scripts/strip-native.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# AREA — native binary stripping + optional packing.
#
# Removes symbols, build-id, and (where present) metadata sections that feed
# REA's inspect_binary_layout / inspect_elf_notes / inspect_macho /
# inspect_rust_binary / inspect_pe_imports.
#
# Usage:
#   ./strip-native.sh /path/to/binary [--upx]
set -euo pipefail

BIN="${1:-}"
UPX="${2:-}"

if [[ -z "$BIN" || ! -f "$BIN" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 /path/to/binary [--upx]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

echo "== Stripping $BIN"

# Full symbol stripping (works on ELF and Mach-O).
strip -S -x -s "$BIN" 2>/dev/null || strip "$BIN" || echo "  (strip not available; continuing)"

# Remove GNU build-id and note sections (ELF).
for sec in .note.gnu.build-id .note.ABI-tag .dep-v0 .comment; do
  if objcopy --remove-section="$sec" "$BIN" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "  removed section $sec"
  fi
done

# Rust cargo-auditable metadata (defeats inspect_rust_binary).
strip -R .dep-v0 "$BIN" 2>/dev/null || true

# Go build metadata (defeats inspect_go_binary).
if command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  go tool buildid -w "$BIN" 2>/dev/null && echo "  cleared go build id" || true
fi

if [[ "$UPX" == "--upx" ]]; then
  if command -v upx >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    upx --best --lzma "$BIN" && echo "  packed with upx"
  else
    echo "  (upx not found; skipping pack)" >&2
  fi
fi

echo "== Done. Verify with: rea open_binary $BIN && analyze_function"

```
